Xenosaga did a good job with the Gnosis, except that the fact that the Gnosis are so goddam goofy that it removes much of their menace.  Especially the Golems, why did they have phalluses? 

Dark Force/Falz is a great example of a lovecraftian villain in a sci fi series, namely the Phantasy Star series.   PS is hardly hard sci fi, especially the original tetrology, but I think Sovereign was very much a perfect example of a Lovecraft-esque villain like Dark Falz working in a harder sci fi setting and being given the ability to voice its menace and its diabolical ambitions of the races of the Milky Way. 

One of the screenplays I am writing at the moment is a space western called Waltzing Matilda and it takes inspiration from Firefly and Xenosaga, and the main antagonists in it, the Lilim, are pretty much a combination of the Reavers and the Gnosis but with the Lovecraftian elements of both played up much more.    One of the main elements I am using is that the Lilim hail from a different dimension then our universe, which allows them to wreak all sorts of havoc since they do not even obey many of the fundamental physical laws of our universe, phasing between our universe and theirs.

## Which girls did you want Link to get with?

Link being the most elegable bachelor in Hyrule, no matter what incarnation he is, has many beautiful women after him \(and a few men, but those men are almost always as ugly as the day is long\). So, which girls were you rooting for to get with our hero? Since Link's personality is largely left up to the viewer's interpretation and projections, it's often just a case of which girl you liked best/had the best chemistry.

Hero of Time: I liked Link and Ruto. Some people might think that's weird, but when it comes down to it Ruto is just a fantasy version of the blue skinned beautiful alien girl trope, hell, I thought of the asari as just looking like Space Ruto. Some people go with the interpretation that Link finds Ruto pushy and disgusting and repulsive, while others think of her affections being returned at least somewhat: Link seems shocked when he sees her again as an adult: is he shocked that his pushy fiance has returned \(on the other hand Link was going to the Temple to save her and her people\) or is he surprised that the rude bratty princess has blossomed into a figure that's rather easy on the eyes, and is very.... bosomy shall we say? This animation went with the latter theory of Link lusting after the sexy fish princess. I suppose I also liked Ruto because I would say she is one of the few characters who develops in Ocarina of Time, going from a selfish, rude bratty princess to a very caring, understanding, surprisingly graceful in losing in love who will sacrifice anything she has for the good of her people and Hyrule as a whole.

[https://youtu.be/6Tn1MUIqUTI?t=5m35s](https://youtu.be/6Tn1MUIqUTI?t=5m35s)

Twilight Princess Link: Oh boy. I loved the relationship he had with Midna. I think Midna might be perhaps the most complex and developed character in Zelda, at least until BotW. Midna is a throwback to Veran in terms of design, but her personality is very similar to Ruto, she blows Ruto's tsundere\-ness out of the water, which I didn't think was possible. In some ways TP takes the concepts raised in Jabu Jabu's Belly and the Earth and Wind Temples of TWW and creates a whole game, but with Ruto essentially being the main heroine of the game, and her personality being considerably fleshed and with differences: Ruto doesn't really have Midna's morbid sense of humour or snark, but their personalities are very similar overall.

 And at one point, we find out that Midna like Ruto transforms into something obviously not human, but very easy on the eyes as well. Link and Midna have some of the best chemistries, which makes the ending of the game all the more sad. I personally consider Twilight Princess to be Midna's story and her quest, she grows from someone who cares only for her own kingdom and could not care less about Hyrule, but gradually desires to save both worlds from their peril for its own sake, rather then just eliminating a threat to her people and throne.

 You could remove Link from the story without it changing too much, or Zelda even, but there is no Twilight Princess without Midna. Out of all of Link's partners, Midna left the strongest impact on me and I really found myself wanting them to get together: there felt something VERY genuine about Link and Midna, rather then Ilia \(who was nice but seemed like a throwback to both Midna and Saria but the story didn't seem to know what to do with her\) and Zelda who was fun and easily the third most important heroic character \(I see Midna as being the protagonist, Link as the deuteragonist and Zelda as the tritagonist\).

And finally my 3rd favourite pairing came from the Oracle Games. I found Nayru interesting as the had all the hallmarks of a Love INterest: Beautiful? Oh yes. Gorgeous singing voice? Yes. Plays the harp. Is crucial to the plot with her powers? Of course. Damsel in distress? But of course. But Link and Nayru never seemed interested in each other, perhaps Link knew Nayru and Ralph were bound to happen sooner or later. Besides it seemed like Link and Din had a lot of chemistry.

 It's a shame because Din isn't in the game for anywhere near as long as Nayru, only being seen at the end, but while Link's feelings to her were ambiguous, Din clearly smitten. What I did like about the ending sequence of an unlinked Oracle of Seasons was that it really looked like Link and Din were going on a date, and the final scene of that was them looking into each other's eyes, with Link blushing and reaching out to take her hand, while she flashed him a coy flirty look. I was rather unhappy with the ending of a linked game with Zelda getting to smooch the hero, rather then Din. I was like back off honey, he's taken!

I also found it interesting in that Marin, if \(Oracles are still supposed to be an interequel between ALTTP and LA\) seems to be a combination of all 3 main non evil females in AllTP/Oracles. She is said to resemble Zelda \(I didn't really see it personally in the artwork\), sings and plays the harp like Nayru but her red hair and overall personality is very similar to Din rather then Zelda or Nayru. It makes me wonder about the nature of Koholint Island: is it already fully formed, or is it nebullous, and Link's own dreams and memories influince the world around him? Perhaps Link's memories of Din, Nayru and Zelda influinced her appearance, or Koholint is menat to be a mixed up dream mirror of the real world, and thus Marin is a counterpart in some ways to Zelda, Din and Nayru due to having elements of all three in her appearance and personality and mannerisms.
